<description>
`-bytespersigop` is parsed as int64, stored as unsigned int, and multiplied by a transaction's sigop cost into the int32 sizes used by the mempool. Negative values wrap, values of 2^32 or more are truncated (4294967296 turns the sigop adjustment off), and large values overflow, so a debug build aborts on an `Assume`. The first commit refuses any value outside [0, 21474] at startup: up to 21474, a package of 25 transactions at the standard sigops limit still has an int32 size.

The second commit checks the sigops limit before a transaction is staged. A transaction that is otherwise standard can be far over that limit, and at 21474 one with about 100,000 sigops still overflows when staged. `mempool_sigoplimit.py` covers the range, a 25-transaction package at 21474, and that transaction.
</description>

<commits>
fac9c100c7 init: refuse -bytespersigop values that overflow

-bytespersigop is parsed as int64_t and stored in an unsigned int, so
a negative value wraps and a value of 2^32 or more is truncated: -1
becomes 4294967295, and 4294967296 becomes 0, which silently turns off
the sigop adjustment.

The stored value is then multiplied by the sigop cost of a transaction
into sigop-adjusted sizes, and these are narrowed to int32_t: the weight
used by TxGraph, and the total vsize of a package in CheckFeeRate. A
standard transaction has a sigop cost of at most
MAX_STANDARD_TX_SIGOPS_COST (16000), so its vsize is at most
16000 * bytespersigop / WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR (4), and a package holds at
most MAX_PACKAGE_COUNT (25) transactions. The package total fits in
int32_t while 25 * 4000 * bytespersigop <= INT32_MAX (2147483647), that
is up to 21474: 100000 * 21474 = 2147400000, while
100000 * 21475 = 2147500000 does not fit. Above that, a package of 25
transactions at the limit aborts a debug build on
Assume(virtual_bytes >= 0) in CFeeRate::GetFee; above 134217, so does a
single transaction, on Assume(feerate.size > 0) in
TxGraphImpl::AddTransaction.

Refuse at startup any value outside [0, 21474], before it is stored.

7d37a758b3 validation: check sigops limit before staging

PreChecks stages a transaction in the mempool changeset before it
checks MAX_STANDARD_TX_SIGOPS_COST. The bound on -bytespersigop keeps
sigop-adjusted sizes in int32_t only for transactions within that
limit. A transaction that is otherwise standard can be far above it:
two P2WSH inputs with 50020 sigops each are 1365 vbytes. At
-bytespersigop=21474, 100040 * 21474 = 2148258960 exceeds INT32_MAX,
and staging it fails Assume(feerate.size > 0) in
TxGraphImpl::AddTransaction, which aborts a debug build.

Check the limit right after counting the sigops, before staging.
</commits>
